classification.theory_summary: Proposes that recurring mall/school labyrinth dreams come from childhood first experiences of massive public interiors; dreams reuse these spatial memories to convey anxiety/wonder.
classification.skip_reason: No specific dream episode, locations visited, events, or sensory details—post is a general theory about why mall/school spaces appear in dreams.

meta.author_theory: Malls/schools/large labyrinth interiors resonate due to early childhood exposure to vast overstimulating spaces; dreams transform abstract emotions into visual/spatial/tactile forms using memory; these spaces convey anxiety or wonder in adulthood.

extraction.extraction_notes: Phenomenological extraction not applicable: the post contains generalized descriptions of place-types (malls, schools, large labyrinth interiors) but no concrete dream scene with describable light, crowding, specific rooms, movement, entities, or events.
